Let \(p(x)\) be a polynomial with real coefficients. The number of positive real roots of \(p(x)\) is at most the number of sign changes in the sequence of its coefficients, and the number of negative real roots is at most the number of sign changes in the sequence of coefficients of \(p(-x)\).

theorem descartes_rule_of_signs:
assumes "p ≠ 0"
shows "positive_roots ≤ sign_changes(coefficients p)"
and "negative_roots ≤ sign_changes(coefficients p(-x))"
